newsitem.title: USA: 'Babe' actor saves Florida pig from slaughter.
newsitem.headline: 'Babe' actor saves Florida pig from slaughter.

text.p: Mr. D isn't the kind of pig to herd sheep or chat up a duck but that didn't stop Farmer Hoggett of "Babe" fame from stepping in to save his life.

At the behest of a national animal rights organisation, actor James Cromwell, who starred as Farmer Hoggett in the popular film, rescued the 240-pound boar from the butcher's block and set him up in cushy retirement, a Florida animal sanctuary said on Wednesday.
In "Babe," Hoggett befriended a cute little pig and taught it to herd sheep as well as a dog. In real life, Cromwell bought a pig that was raised by students as a 4-H project.
"I'm happy to buy (Mr. D) to save him from slaughter," the actor said in a written statement released by People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals.
Mr. D was auctioned off last week at a youth fair where money raised goes back into student projects. Normally, the next stop for Mr. D would have been the slaughter house.
PETA raised $1,700 in an effort to save the pig, the Ocala Star-Banner newspaper said, but the high bid was $5,000. PETA convinced the new owner to sell Mr. D at a loss.

Cromwell agreed to reimburse PETA for the pig and pay for his food, a pen and swimming pool at the All Creatures Sanctuary in Ocklawaha, Florida, Tish Hennessey, director of the foundation that supports the sanctuary, said.
